definition: Small per-step errors accumulating over a multi-step rollout until the trajectory is wrong, and across 3 sources the limit that bounds latent and iterative methods specifically. Its instances: auxiliary objectives for multi-step latent prediction either have a limited horizon or accumulate error over the rollout, which is the trade one hierarchical method is built against; a formal treatment of latent chain-of-thought bounds what continuous rollouts can achieve; and, in discrete traces, one source finds a model's first solution usually its best with later alternatives actively harmful, characterising the errors as a forest and pruning accordingly. The archive's related material supplies the same shape in other settings -- iterative refinement accumulating into global-shape drift in forecasting, and repeated local corrections distorting a long-horizon trend.

evidence.note: Adds a higher-level abstract latent as an auxiliary pretraining target to reduce compounding error in latent-space rollouts, aiming at longer-horizon coherence than multi-token or next-latent prediction.
evidence.title: Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models

evidence.note: Finds that a reasoning model's first solution is usually its best and that later alternatives are actively harmful, characterizes the errors as a forest structure, and prunes accordingly.
evidence.title: FoE: Forest of Errors Makes the First Solution the Best in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Explains why latent chain-of-thought excels at exploration but fails at computation by identifying decisional certainty as the governing variable, formalizing it as the Symbolic Index, and proving that curriculum learning is not merely helpful but necessary for training latent reasoners.
evidence.title: Capabilities and Fundamental Limits of Latent Chain-of-Thought

name: compounding error
